subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: Should OpenClaw solve the remaining Codex-OAuth sibling-quota fallback by adding Harmony function-call support to the direct OpenClaw Responses runtime, by pursuing an upstream Codex app-server/session fix, or by limiting current work to the model-scoped quota bookkeeping in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99810?
rationale: The source evidence shows real gaps in both current bookkeeping and direct-runtime tool-call handling, but the durable owner boundary depends on whether maintainers want the Codex app-server or the direct runtime to be the supported Codex-OAuth tool path.

options.title: Stage bookkeeping, then decide runtime owner
options.body: Review the linked bookkeeping PR first, require a live app-server/direct-runtime repro for the remaining 429 split, and only add Harmony direct-runtime support if maintainers choose that as a supported Codex path.

options.title: Fix upstream Codex/app-server behavior
options.body: Keep Codex models on the app-server path and investigate session or WebSocket reuse against upstream Codex before adding a second OpenClaw parser path.

options.title: Make direct OpenClaw runtime the fallback target
options.body: Add a focused Harmony function-call adapter and regression/live proof so direct `openclaw` can run Codex-OAuth models with tools when app-server quota behavior is wrong.

recommendation.title: Stage bookkeeping, then decide runtime owner
recommendation.body: Review the linked bookkeeping PR first, require a live app-server/direct-runtime repro for the remaining 429 split, and only add Harmony direct-runtime support if maintainers choose that as a supported Codex path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the extracted AI runtime, Codex app-server harness, and OpenAI provider boundary where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
